title: Back to the Future
facts: Robert Zemeckis directed the film and wrote it with Bob Gale.
Steven Spielberg was an executive producer.
Eric Stoltz was first cast as Marty McFly. Michael J. Fox replaced him several weeks into filming.
Michael J. Fox filmed the TV series Family Ties by day and Back to the Future at night.
The time machine is a DeLorean DMC-12.
The time machine needs 1.21 gigawatts of power and a speed of 88 miles per hour.
"The Power of Love" by Huey Lewis and the News was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song.
Huey Lewis appears as the judge who tells Marty's band it is "just too darn loud".
Back to the Future was the highest-grossing film of 1985.
The film won the Academy Award for Best Sound Effects Editing.
The Hill Valley town square is a set on the Universal Studios backlot.
Doc Brown's dog is named Einstein in 1985. His dog in 1955 is named Copernicus.
Crispin Glover plays George McFly. Lea Thompson plays Lorraine.
Back to the Future opened in the United States on July 3, 1985.
In 2007 the Library of Congress selected the film for the National Film Registry.
Twin Pines Mall becomes Lone Pine Mall after Marty runs over a pine tree in 1955.
In early drafts of the script, the time machine was a refrigerator.
